==English==
{{was wotd|2008|December|18}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*delh₁-}}
From {{bor|en|fr|indolent}} or directly from {{bor|en|la-lat|indolēns}}, from {{prefix|la|in-|t1=not|dolēns|t2=hurting|nocat=1}}, from {{m|la|doleo|t=to hurt}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''adj.'' and ''n.''|noformat=1|id=1139300201}}</ref><ref name="Online Etymology Dictionary">{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary|pos=adj}}</ref> The later sense of “living easily, slothful” perhaps developed in French.<ref name="Online Etymology Dictionary"/>

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɪn.də.lənt/|a=UK,US}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-indolent.ogg|a=US}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# [[habitually|Habitually]] [[lazy]], [[procrastinate|procrastinating]], or [[resistant]] to [[physical]] [[labor]].
#: {{ux|en|The '''indolent''' girl resisted doing her homework.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1815
|author=w:Jane Austen
|title=w:Emma
|volume=II
|section=chapter 18
|passage=Mr. Churchill has pride; but his pride is nothing to his wife’s: his is a quiet, '''indolent''', gentlemanlike sort of pride that would harm nobody, and only make himself a little helpless and tiresome; but her pride is arrogance and insolence!}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1978|last=Kołakowski|first=Leszek|authorlink=Leszek Kołakowski|title=w:Main Currents of Marxism|volume=II: The Golden Age|origlang=pl|original=Główne nurty marksizmu: rozwój|translator=P[aul] S[teven] Falla|origyear=1976|publisher=w:Clarendon Press|location=w:Oxford|isbn=9780198245698|oclc=961252281|page=466|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/maincurrentsofma00lesz/page/466|passage={{...}} the obscurities of his text are not due so much to inherent philosophical difficulties as to Lenin's '''indolent''' and superficial approach and his contempt for all problems that could not be put to direct use in the struggle for power.}}
# [[induce|Inducing]] [[laziness]].
#: {{ux|en|'''indolent''' comfort}}
# {{lb|en|medicine}} Causing little or no physical [[pain]]; [[progress]]ing slowly; [[inactive]] (of an [[ulcer]], etc.).
# {{lb|en|medicine}} [[heal|Healing]] slowly.

====Synonyms====
* {{l|en|idle}}, {{l|en|work-shy}}; see also [[Thesaurus:lazy]]
